To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose WO-Join, a novel data-driven join scheme that dynamically adjusts the buffer size according to input characteristics; 2) our evaluation shows that WO-Join produces higher quality results and lower memory costs compared to W-Join; 3) WO-Join also has better performance in terms of latency and throughput.
a data-driven memory-management scheme can be used in stream joins to improve performance and that the scheme is particularly effective in ordered or partially-ordered data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) What is a good memory management scheme for stream join?
the design of a data-driven memory manager that can adaptively allocate and release the memory for a stream join.

the following: 1) how to design a data-driven memory manager that adapts to the input stream, 2) how to design the data-driven scheme in a way that it can be integrated into existing stream processing systems, and 3) how to implement the scheme to minimize the overhead.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our data-driven memory management approach can improve the quality of results and reduce the memory costs of stream joins.
WO-Join outperforms W-Join in most cases and produces higher quality results.
our proposed WO-Join approach provides a more robust solution than W-Join for the problem of memory management of stream joins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a novel data-driven join scheme, WO-Join, for ordered or partially ordered inputs and demonstrated its superior performance over the traditional W-Join.
, for ordered streams, we should not be so obsessed with the window size.
WO-Join can be viewed as an adaptive memory management mechanism for stream join that is more robust than the traditional W-Join.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the memory management scheme should be data-driven, rather than query-driven.
the memory management for stateful operators should be data-driven instead of query-driven.
, when the input stream is ordered or partially ordered (which is often the case), a data-driven memory allocation scheme can achieve better performance than a query-driven one.
